title: Derived sections of the integral dual tensor a classical torsion heart object
statement: Let l be prime and E/Q_l a finite extension. On a Noetherian scheme S let L be an integral module object with a finite constant local model [det-lem-int-ext-formula], and suppose s in N equals cd_l(S) [sk-def-cd]. For every integral module sheaf F whose underlying abelian sheaf is classical and locally l-power torsion, RGamma(S, D tensor^L F[0]) has cohomology in [0,s+1], where D is the actual integralStratumDual l E S L and tensor and sections are integralStratumDualTensor and integralStratumDerivedSections [det-lem-int-ext-formula]. No constructibility of F or common exponent of annihilation is assumed.

source.place: paragraph (2), second and third bullets, applied to a heart object

proof.text: The finite constant local model has a two-term finite-free integral resolution. The DVR property gives the free kernel. Its completed extension is flat. Evaluation identifies the reversed dual complex with the actual derived dual. It has Tor amplitude [0,1], so tensor with F[0] has no cohomology outside [0,1].

First suppose F is annihilated by one prime power. A corresponding finite uniformizer quotient of the dual has a finite-free constant local model, hence is constructible and classical. Descend it and F to bounded-below etale complexes. Finite Tor reflection and tensor pullback identify their tensor with the recorded integral tensor after scalar restriction. Thus its cohomology is classical and torsion. For general F, exact filtered colimits of its prime-power kernels give the same assertion, since derived tensor and comparison inverse image preserve them. No inverse limit is used.

source.place: paragraph (2), second bullet; parent step 8, specialized to a heart object

proof.text: For each of its two cohomology sheaves, compare module-derived and abelian-derived sections via finite-coefficient comparison (first at each exponent, then the torsion colimit). The definition of s bounds these in [0,s]. The finite truncation triangles and their long exact sequences give [0,s+1] for derived sections of the tensor. Empty S and zero sheaves give zero complexes.

source.place: paragraph (2), third bullet; parent step 9, applied to [0,1]

mathlib_searches.query: Hom from a stratum extension to derived finite reductions vanishes above cohomological dimension
mathlib_searches.results: DerivedCategory.isZero_of_isLE/isGE and projective/injective single-complex Hom vanishings; these do not give the geometric input.

lean.statement:
theorem integral_dual_torsion_heart_sections
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian S]
    (L : pulledBackModuleObjects (integralCoefficientRing l E) S)
    (hmodel : HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (integralCoefficientRing l E) S L)
    (s : ℕ)
    (hs : (s : WithTop ℕ) = cohomologicalDimension l (Fact.out : l.Prime) S)
    (F : pulledBackModuleObjects (integralCoefficientRing l E) S)
    (hF : IsClassicalAbelian F.X)
    (htors : IsEllPowerTorsion l (Fact.out : l.Prime) F.X) :
    ∀ q : ℤ, q < 0 ∨ (s : ℤ) + 1 < q →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Ab.{u + 1} q).obj
        ((integralStratumDerivedSections l E S).obj
          ((integralStratumDualTensor l E S L).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F))))
